description: Scenarios selected from the upstream pandas asv benchmark suite (tag v3.1.0). Each scenario runs one upstream class/parameter combination with a fixed random seed and a pinned iteration count, so the published wall time is the per-call mean of an asv-style batch.

criteria: benchmark definitions are the upstream asv benchmarks of pandas 3.1.0
the benchmark data are generated locally (no download at measurement time)
one fixed parameter combination per scenario so every sample runs the same code
one timed call stays well below one second so a batch of iterations measures a stable mean

excluded.benchmarks.io.parsers: the upstream parser benchmark only ships datetime-inference micro cases
excluded.benchmarks.io.csv: the CSV benchmarks synthesise files under /tmp and spend most of their time in file system calls
excluded.benchmarks.io.excel: requires openpyxl/xlsxwriter, which are not part of the pinned runtime
excluded.benchmarks.io.sql: requires SQLAlchemy and a database server
excluded.benchmarks.arithmetic: mostly numexpr-gated and imports optional acceleration packages
excluded.benchmarks.categoricals: its largest cases are sub-millisecond and duplicate the groupby coverage
excluded.benchmarks.libs: benchmarks third-party libraries rather than pandas itself

scenarios.notes: 1e6 rows, one million distinct keys, groupby sum with sort=True; exercises the hash table plus the unique-key safe sort.
~650k rows with duplicated integer index columns; groupby max over five columns, a regression guard for the int64 overflow path.
100k row frame joined against a 1000 row indexed lookup table on a single key, sorted output.
200k vs 1e6 row frames, asof join on integer time keys with backward direction; exercises the merge_asof search path.
100k x 4 float frame, per-column skew over axis 0; the slowest of the upstream frame reduction kernels.
100k row float frame, rolling window of 1000, mean reduction; checks the rolling kernel against a numpy window mean.
1e6 row single integer column with 10k distinct values; drop_duplicates keeps the first occurrence of every key.
10k x 4 frame on a two-level MultiIndex, unstack of the second level into a 100 x 400 wide frame.
10k element object-dtype string series, vectorised str.upper; representative of the pandas 3 string dtype path.
